method: Capacity: the aggregate demand is the peak device count times the target throughput per device in Mbps; the usable throughput of one access point is its throughput after the headroom percentage is held back; the number of access points for capacity is the demand divided by that usable throughput, rounded up. Coverage: the floor area in square metres divided by the coverage area of one access point, rounded up. The plan takes the larger of the two counts, so a capacity-limited plan runs at 100% minus the headroom in airtime when every client asks for its full target, and a coverage-limited plan carries less load per access point. Inputs: floor area 1 to 100000 m2, devices a whole number from 1 to 100000, target throughput 0.1 to 10000 Mbps, usable throughput per AP 1 to 10000 Mbps, coverage area per AP 1 to 20000 m2, and headroom 0 to 50 percent. Throughput values are rounded half up to one decimal, counts are exact integers, and a plan never drops below one access point. The capacity model is a first-pass budget: it assumes uniform device demand and a uniform coverage cell. The optional coverage sketch stores building width and depth (2 to 100 metres), up to 6 floors, 64 access points and 200 partitions. Estimated received signal is transmit power minus the configured loss at 1 metre, 10 times the path-loss exponent times the base-10 logarithm of three-dimensional distance in metres (with a 1-metre minimum), minus 12 dB per wall, 6 dB per door, 3 dB per window and 20 dB per concrete partition crossed on the same floor, and minus the configured 0 to 40 dB for each floor crossed. Cross-floor paths omit partitions. The heatmap selects the strongest access point at each sample and reports the percentage meeting a configurable target from -90 to -40 dBm. Defaults are 20 dBm transmit power, 46 dB reference loss, exponent 3, -67 dBm target, 3-metre floor spacing and 15 dB loss per floor. This comparative model does not include antenna patterns, frequency-specific material response, reflection, interference, roaming, client capability or a site survey; measured results can differ. Capacity calculations and coverage sketches run entirely in the browser with no network access. A sketch remains in memory unless the visitor explicitly saves it in local browser storage or downloads or imports the versioned JSON design file; files are limited to 256 KiB and validated locally.

sources.title: IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN capacity planning: aggregate offered load divided by usable per-access-point throughput
Enterprise WLAN design guidance: cell size and client density, typically 150 to 250 square metres per access point in open-plan offices
Wi-Fi airtime efficiency: usable application throughput is roughly 40 to 60 percent of the PHY rate after contention, management traffic and retries
Log-distance path-loss model: distance-dependent attenuation plus explicit partition and floor losses
